fieldMarks: Looks like a small Canada goose with a very short, stubby bill.
Smallest forms are barely larger than a mallard.
Sexes look alike; males slightly larger.
behavior: Higher-pitched honk than the Canada goose and high cackling calls.
Grazes on land and dips its head in water; eats grasses, sedges, aquatic plants and waste grain in fields.
Strongly migratory; Alaskan birds winter mainly in California, central Canadian Arctic birds on the southern Great Plains and near the western Gulf Coast.
habitat: Breeds on tundra; winters on southern lakes and marshes, often foraging in open prairie and farm fields.
range: Breeds in western Alaska, the Aleutians and north-central Arctic Canada; winters in California, the southern Great Plains and near the western Gulf Coast.

lookalikes.name: Canada goose
lookalikes.howToTell: The Canada goose is larger with a longer bill and a lower honk.
